note: Corps of Engineers campground on the Illinois bank of the Mississippi just above Lock and Dam 14, between Hampton and Port Byron. The west loop's sites sit by a riprap bank on the open river; a marsh lies in front of the east loop. No river access from the campground; the day-use area next door has fishing spots and a canoe ramp. The Mississippi River Trail passes the entrance, and a rail line runs along the landward side. --Claude
summary: rec.gov facility, rates, catalog (56 sites) and availability read: 46 electric RV sites (50 A, no water/sewer) + 5 tent; all back-ins, fit 20-70 ft (stored 80 was a driveway length); $26 (2027; tents $14); season 05-01..10-23; reservation only (fcfs never); showers, flush toilets, dump, water. RIVERFRONT KEPT: west-loop sites 008, 009, 011, 012, 013 are 17-26 m from the open Mississippi (Pool 14, ~1 km wide, main river not a slough) over grass and scattered trees to a riprap bank; no levee. Count 51 -> 46 (RV). Pin and phone fine.
flags: WATERFRONT (stored riverfront, KEPT with a riprap caveat): measured to the 173.8 m Pool 14 surface (3DEP) and on Esri z19: 013 (41.569322,-90.392386) 17 m, 012 (41.569086,-90.392452) 22 m, 009 (41.569444,-90.392024) 25 m, 011 (41.56941,-90.392141) 25 m, 008 (41.569473,-90.39189) 26 m; ~1 m above pool, over grass with scattered large trees to a riprap band. All five are reservable nightly sites (none of the five closed ones). The water is the main Mississippi pool just above L&D 14, ~1 km wide, not a backwater slough; no levee between sites and river (rail line and IL-84 are on the landward side). rec.gov itself says 'there is no river access from within the campground' (riprap). The east loop (026-051) faces a cattail marsh: view at best.
